blocks.text: The “twentieth year” in verse 1 is conventionally dated to 445/444 BCE by identifying the king as Artaxerxes I. The exact year remains disputed, since different ways of reckoning a king’s accession and the calendar can produce variations.

The first-person voice introduced here continues through vivid accounts of court life, building, prayer, opposition, and reform. Yet the book also includes third-person narration, lists, material concerning Ezra, and editorial transitions. The book therefore cannot be explained simply as either a complete autobiography or a wholly fictionalized account.

The mourning, fasting, confession, and request for favor in this chapter lead into action: Nehemiah plans, asks Artaxerxes for authorization, and receives letters and access to timber. The prayer is thus part of the movement toward the work that follows.
